editorial.headline: Metal Construction Wholesale: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale metal construction materials are open to full foreign ownership nationally, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration.
editorial.body:
Wholesale metal construction materials are the practical subject of this activity. It covers wholesale trade in metal building materials, from wire rope and insect-screen wire to nails, nuts, bolts, hinges, latches, locks and keys. Water tanks, water towers, rolling doors and awnings are equally within the recorded scope. These examples give the category its commercial texture: a wholesale activity concerned with the metal components and installations used in construction, access, storage and cover. Its identity is broad enough to hold those varied goods together, yet specific in its focus on wholesale trade in metal construction materials.

The record makes the activity available at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. This is not a category held back for only the largest wholesale houses, nor is it framed as an activity confined to the smallest operators. The same stated scope is open at each of the four scales. That matters because the register speaks in terms of one coherent wholesale activity, even as the catalogued goods range from fasteners and hardware to tanks, towers, rolling doors and awnings. Scale availability therefore does not alter the activity’s essential description; the core remains wholesale trade in the listed metal construction materials.

Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In national terms, foreign capital is therefore not capped below full ownership for this activity. But the national setting is not the Bali answer. Bali marks the activity Blocked (risk class) and records it as blocked: a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. That is the central distinction. National openness describes the national position for the activity; the Bali status determines whether a PMA registration can proceed on the island.

Bali’s block is tied to risk classification, not to a separate Bali foreign-ownership ceiling. At the Besar scale, OSS classifies every scope in the activity as Low or Medium-Low risk. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, bringing this activity within its reach. The record dates that moratorium to May 2026. The conclusion for a founder is deliberately plain: this is a nationally open wholesale activity, open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar, but it is blocked from PMA registration in Bali under the provincial moratorium.
